runtimes.name: WebLLM (MLC) @mlc-ai/web-llm v0.2.85
runtimes.requirements: Needs WebGPU (navigator.gpu plus a working requestAdapter()). Browsers: Chrome/Edge 113+ on Windows, macOS and ChromeOS; Chrome 121+ on Android 12+ (Qualcomm/ARM GPUs); Safari 26+ on macOS/iOS/iPadOS; Firefox 141+ on Windows (other OSes behind flags). Models with the q4f16 / q0f16 quant need the adapter feature 'shader-f16' (config.ts sets required_features:['shader-f16'] on 29 records). Without it, use the q4f32 variants. vram_required_MB is MLC's own estimate for weights, KV cache and buffers at the default context (4096; the '-1k' variants use 1024). Some records have buffer_size_required_bytes, which is checked against adapter.limits.maxStorageBufferBindingSize. low_resource_required=true means MLC considers the model OK for limited devices such as Android phones. Weights are cached in the Cache API / IndexedDB, so the origin needs roughly the model size in storage quota (navigator.storage.estimate()). No COOP/COEP needed.
runtimes.notes: Source: raw.githubusercontent.com/mlc-ai/web-llm/main/src/config.ts, fetched 2026-09-29, npm package.json version 0.2.85. The file has 165 records: 161 LLM/VLM plus 4 embedding models. The embedding records have no low_resource_required field; they are listed here as false. Newest families in the list: Qwen3.5 (0.8B/2B/4B/9B), Ministral-3-3B (2512), Qwen3, gemma3-1b, Phi-4-mini, DeepSeek-R1 distills. It does NOT include Gemma 3n/4, Llama 4, gpt-oss or Qwen3-VL. Qwen3.5 records set context_window_size 4096 and max_history_size 1. The 70B q3f16 needs about 31 GB of VRAM, which in practice means a 48GB+ Apple-silicon Mac only. The app can import prebuiltAppConfig at runtime (CDN esm.run/@mlc-ai/web-llm) and read model_list directly instead of hard-coding it. Rule of thumb for 'fits here': vram_required_MB < ~70% of estimated GPU memory, or of system RAM on unified-memory devices. On iOS Safari, per-tab memory limits (~1.5-3 GB, depending on device RAM) make anything above ~2 GB risky.

runtimes.name: Transformers.js (Hugging Face) v4 (latest tag 4.3.0; v4.0 released 2026-02-09)
runtimes.requirements: Pipeline option device: 'webgpu' | 'wasm' (default in browser) | 'webnn' variants. Pipeline option dtype: 'fp32' | 'fp16' | 'q8' (int8/uint8) | 'q4' | 'q4f16' | 'bnb4'. WASM backend: runs in every modern browser including Safari/iOS and Firefox, but is limited by the wasm32 heap (4 GB max; 2 GB ArrayBuffer/protobuf limit per ONNX file, larger models use external-data sharding) and needs COOP/COEP headers for multithreading. WebGPU backend: needs navigator.gpu; fp16/q4f16 need the 'shader-f16' adapter feature. v4 ships a rewritten C++ WebGPU runtime (with ONNX Runtime) that also runs in Node/Bun/Deno. v4 supports models over 8B params; the HF demo shows GPT-OSS-20B q4f16 at ~60 tok/s on an M4 Pro/Max. Models must be ONNX exports, usually under the onnx-community/ or Xenova/ HF orgs.
runtimes.notes: Typical models and dtypes (sizes approximate for the given dtype, medium confidence). Whisper: onnx-community/whisper-base / whisper-small / whisper-large-v3-turbo, q4/fp16, ~80 MB to ~1 GB. Moonshine for ASR. Kokoro-82M TTS (onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX, q8 ~90 MB). Chatterbox TTS. Embeddings: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, bge / gte, EmbeddingGemma-300M. LLMs: SmolLM2/SmolLM3-3B, Qwen2.5/Qwen3-0.6B-4B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Phi-3.5/Phi-4-mini, Gemma-3-270M/1B, Gemma 3n, LFM2, Granite-4.0 (GraniteMoeHybrid), gpt-oss-20b (q4f16, ~12-13 GB VRAM). Vision: Florence-2, SmolVLM, Janus, depth-anything, RMBG background removal, Segment Anything. Rule: WebGPU q4f16 size ≈ params × 0.55-0.6 bytes. WASM is realistic only up to ~1-2B params (q4/q8), and only for small models on phones.

runtimes.name: ONNX Runtime Web (onnxruntime-web) v1.30.0
runtimes.requirements: Execution providers: 'wasm' (CPU, SIMD; multithreaded only when the page is crossOriginIsolated through COOP/COEP headers), 'webgpu' (needs navigator.gpu; Chrome/Edge 113+, Safari 26+, Firefox 141+ on Windows), 'webnn' (Chrome/Edge behind flags or origin trial; Windows DirectML/NPU, ChromeOS, macOS Core ML). Memory: wasm32 build limited to 4 GB linear memory, and a single protobuf model file is limited to 2 GB, so larger models need external data files. ORT publishes a wasm64/Memory64 build (JSEP) for >4 GB, which requires a browser with Memory64 (Chrome 133+ / Firefox 134+; Safari not yet). This is the engine under transformers.js.
runtimes.notes: Latest git tag v1.30.0 (checked 2026-09-29). Microsoft Edge docs point to ORT Web and WebNN as alternatives to the built-in Prompt API. Treat ORT Web as the backend that powers transformers.js and many demo sites, not as a runtime end users pick directly.

runtimes.name: MediaPipe LLM Inference API for Web (@mediapipe/tasks-genai) -> successor LiteRT-LM JS
runtimes.requirements: Requires WebGPU (mandatory; no CPU/WASM fallback for LLMs). Chrome/Edge desktop is recommended; Android Chrome works for small models. Model files: .litertlm / .task / .bin; web builds are named '-Web' (e.g. gemma-3n-E4B-it-int4-Web.litertlm). Files over 2 GB are streamed or loaded via URL rather than a single ArrayBuffer.
runtimes.notes: Official status: the MediaPipe LLM Inference API is in maintenance-only mode, and Google recommends migrating to the LiteRT-LM JavaScript API. Supported models per docs: Gemma 4 (E2B, E4B), Gemma-3n (E2B, E4B), Gemma-3 (270M, 1B, 4B, 12B, 27B), Gemma-2 2B, Gemma 2B/7B, Phi-2, StableLM, Falcon, MedGemma-27B-Text. Approximate int4 sizes: Gemma-3-1B ~0.55 GB, Gemma-3n-E2B ~3 GB, E4B ~4.4 GB, Gemma-3-4B ~2.6 GB, 12B ~7 GB, 27B ~15 GB (estimates: params × 0.55 bytes, medium confidence).

runtimes.name: wllama (llama.cpp compiled to WebAssembly, with WebGPU) v3.6.1
runtimes.requirements: Runs GGUF files in any browser with WebAssembly (CPU). A multithreaded build is picked automatically when the page is crossOriginIsolated (Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin plus Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp); otherwise it runs single-threaded, which is slow. WebGPU (v3.1+) is enabled automatically and offloads all layers by default. Use n_gpu_layers to partially offload when VRAM is short. Firefox WebGPU works only in compat mode and is much slower. Limits: 'Max file size is 2GB, due to size restriction of ArrayBuffer', so larger GGUFs must be split with llama-gguf-split into chunks of at most 512 MB. The wasm32 build's total heap is capped at 4 GB, so model plus KV cache must fit in under ~4 GB in practice. That means about 3-4B params at Q4 on CPU. Memory64 is not documented in the README. Recommended quants: Q4/Q5/Q6. IQ (imatrix) quants are not recommended because they are slow on CPU.
runtimes.notes: README says v3 adds WebGPU, multimodal and tool calling. Latest tag 3.6.1 (checked 2026-09-29). This is the only in-browser runtime that loads arbitrary HF GGUFs, so it works for the 'run any GGUF under ~4 GB' case. Typical picks: SmolLM2/3, Qwen3-0.6B-4B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Gemma-3-1B/4B, Phi-4-mini at Q4_K_M.

runtimes.name: Chrome built-in AI: Gemini Nano via Prompt API (LanguageModel)
runtimes.requirements: Desktop Google Chrome only (not Chromium distro builds, which lack optimization_guide_internal). OS: Windows 10 or 11; macOS 13+ (Ventura and later); Linux; ChromeOS 16389.0.0+ on Chromebook Plus only. Chrome on Android, Chrome on iOS and non-Plus ChromeOS are not supported. Storage: at least 22 GB free on the volume holding the Chrome profile (the model is removed if space runs low). Hardware, either: GPU with strictly more than 4 GB VRAM, OR CPU inference with 16 GB+ RAM and 4+ CPU cores. Network: unmetered connection for the one-time download (~2.7 GB CPU build / ~4 GB GPU build per adsm.dev). Detection: 'LanguageModel' in self, then await LanguageModel.availability() -> 'unavailable' | 'downloadable' | 'downloading' | 'available'. Multimodal (image/audio) input is supported. Audio input needs the GPU path.
runtimes.notes: Version status conflicts between sources. developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/prompt-api says 'stable in Chrome 138'. That was the extensions release; Summarizer, Translator and Language Detector shipped in 138 for the web. adsm.dev and dev.to report that LanguageModel became enabled by default for web pages in Chrome 148 (2026-05-05). Treat it as: on for the web from Chrome 148, available to extensions from 138. Hardware source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/get-started. The web can't see VRAM, so the app should call availability() instead of guessing. The model is Gemini Nano, not open-weight.

runtimes.name: Microsoft Edge built-in AI: Phi-4-mini (and prerelease Aion-1.0-Instruct) via Prompt API
runtimes.requirements: Developer preview only: Edge Canary/Dev 138.0.3309.2+, with edge://flags 'Prompt API for on-device language model' enabled. Not on by default in Edge Stable. Phi-4-mini requirements: Windows 10 or 11, or macOS 13.3+; at least 20 GB free on the Edge profile volume (the model is deleted below 10 GB); GPU with 5.5 GB+ VRAM; unmetered network. Check edge://on-device-internals: the 'Device performance class' must be High or better. Medium/Low devices can use Aion-1.0-Instruct instead: Edge Canary/Dev 150.0.4070+ with the flag 'Enable prerelease on-device language model'. Aion is smaller, faster and supports weaker GPUs or CPU-only inference. Same LanguageModel API as Chrome.
runtimes.notes: Doc updated 2026-09-02. Microsoft said Aion-1.0-Instruct would be open-sourced in July 2026; this was not verified. Phi-4-mini is 3.8B params, open-weight (MIT), and also available in WebLLM as Phi-4-mini-instruct-q4f16_1-MLC (3437.58 MB).

runtimes.name: Apple Foundation Models framework (Apple Intelligence on-device model)
runtimes.requirements: Native Swift API only; not reachable from a web page. OS: iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS 26+ (framework introduced WWDC25); current release is OS 27. Apple Intelligence must be enabled, with device and Siri language set to the same supported language. Devices: iPhone 15 Pro/Pro Max, all iPhone 16 models (incl. 16e), iPhone 17/17e/17 Pro/17 Pro Max, iPhone Air; iPad with M1 or later and iPad mini (A17 Pro); Mac with M1 or later (and MacBook Neo with A18 Pro); Apple Vision Pro. Storage: up to 14 GB on iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, up to 8 GB on other supported iPhone/iPad/Mac. RAM: 8 GB minimum. iOS 27's larger on-device features need 12 GB (iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, iPhone Air) per MacRumors. Won't run in Game Mode or on low battery.
runtimes.notes: Models: 2025 AFM on-device ~3B params (2-bit QAT). The third generation, announced 2026-06-08 (https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/introducing-third-generation-of-apple-foundation-models), has 'AFM 3 Core' (3B) and 'AFM 3 Core Advanced' (20B sparse, 1-4B active), the latter presumably for 12 GB devices (inference, medium-low confidence). The weights are not open. The web app can only infer eligibility from the UA (iOS 26+, Apple silicon Mac) and tell users apps such as Locally AI or Apple Shortcuts can use it. Siri AI features were not available in the EU at launch of OS 27.

runtimes.name: Ollama
runtimes.requirements: Latest stable tag v0.35.0 (v0.40.0-rc0 in pre-release), checked 2026-09-29. macOS 14 Sonoma+ (Apple silicon uses Metal; Intel Macs CPU only), Windows 10 22H2+/11, Linux x86_64/arm64. NVIDIA: compute capability 5.0+ with driver 550+ (570+ for CC 5.0-6.2). AMD: ROCm v7 on Linux (RX 6000/7000/9000, PRO, Ryzen AI, Instinct); limited Windows support through HIP7. Vulkan backend for Intel/AMD GPUs on Windows/Linux. Rule: RAM/VRAM ≳ GGUF size + 1-2 GB KV cache. 8 GB RAM handles 7-8B Q4; 16 GB handles 14B; 32 GB handles ~30B.
runtimes.notes: GPU docs: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/gpu.mdx. The most popular entry point. Library at ollama.com/library; recommend 'ollama run <model>' commands. Exposes an OpenAI-compatible localhost:11434 API. A web page can detect a running Ollama only if OLLAMA_ORIGINS allows it (CORS).

runtimes.name: LM Studio
runtimes.requirements: macOS: Apple silicon (M1-M4 and later) only, macOS 14.0+, 16 GB+ RAM recommended; Intel Macs not supported. Windows: x64 with AVX2, or ARM64 (Snapdragon X); 16 GB RAM advised; 4 GB+ dedicated VRAM recommended. Linux: AppImage, Ubuntu 20.04+, x64 (AVX2) or ARM64.
runtimes.notes: GUI plus a local server with an OpenAI-compatible API on :1234. Uses llama.cpp (GGUF) everywhere and MLX on Macs. The best recommendation for non-technical desktop users.

runtimes.name: llama.cpp
runtimes.requirements: Rolling bNNNN release builds (prebuilt binaries for Windows CUDA/Vulkan/SYCL/CPU, macOS arm64 Metal, Linux CPU/Vulkan/CUDA/ROCm). Runs on almost anything, including Android via Termux, Raspberry Pi and x86 CPUs without AVX. GGUF quants run from Q2_K to Q8_0/BF16. Memory ≈ file size + KV cache. Supports CPU+GPU split offload (-ngl) and MoE expert offload to CPU (--cpu-moe / -ot), which lets 30B-A3B and gpt-oss-120b-class MoEs run on a 16-24 GB GPU plus 64 GB+ RAM.
runtimes.notes: Underlies Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, GPT4All, PocketPal, LLM Farm and wllama. Also has a WebGPU backend, used in wllama. llama-server includes a built-in web UI.

runtimes.name: MLX / mlx-lm (Apple)
runtimes.requirements: Apple silicon Macs only (M1+), macOS 14+ recommended (13.5 minimum for MLX), Python 3.9+ ('pip install mlx-lm'). Latest mlx-lm tag v0.31.3 (checked 2026-09-29). Uses unified memory. By default macOS caps GPU-wired memory at ~65-75% of RAM (adjustable via sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb). Models from the mlx-community HF org in 3/4/6/8-bit.

guidance:
In-browser checks, run in this order:
1. Look for navigator.gpu. Call requestAdapter({powerPreference:'high-performance'}). Read adapter.features.has('shader-f16'), adapter.limits.maxBufferSize and adapter.limits.maxStorageBufferBindingSize, and adapter.info (vendor/architecture).
2. Read navigator.deviceMemory. Chrome caps it at 8 (older builds) or 32 (newer), and Safari and Firefox don't expose it.
3. Read navigator.hardwareConcurrency.
4. Call navigator.storage.estimate() for the storage quota.
5. Check crossOriginIsolated, which tells you whether WASM threads are available.
6. Check whether 'LanguageModel' in self. If it is, await LanguageModel.availability().
7. Check whether WebAssembly Memory64 validates.

A WebLLM model counts as runnable here when all of these hold:
- WebGPU is present.
- If required_features includes shader-f16, the adapter has it. Otherwise pick the q4f32 twin.
- vram_required_MB is at most about 0.7 × usable GPU memory. On discrete GPUs, VRAM can't be read, so infer it from adapter.info or the WebGL UNMASKED_RENDERER string (for example 'RTX 4060' means 8 GB). On unified-memory devices (Apple silicon, integrated graphics, phones), use about 50-60% of system RAM.
- The storage quota is larger than the model size.

On phones, only offer low_resource_required=true models, and on iOS Safari keep them to about 1.5-2 GB or less because of the tab memory cap.

Suggested verdicts:
- WELL: WebGPU with f16 and the model within budget.
- SLOWLY: WASM-only via wllama or transformers.js (no WebGPU, or WebGPU without f16 so the f32 variant is used) for models of about 1.5B or less at Q4. The same applies when the model fits only with partial offload.
- NOT AT ALL: over the 4 GB wasm32 heap with no WebGPU, or over the budget.

Per device class:
1. Phone
   - iPhone: Safari 26+ has WebGPU, so try WebLLM low_resource models such as SmolLM2-360M, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B q4f16, Llama-3.2-1B and gemma3-1b. Recommend PocketPal AI or Private LLM (App Store). On iPhone 15 Pro and later running iOS 26+, mention that Apple Intelligence / Foundation Models is already on the device.
   - Android: Chrome 121+ with Android 12+ has WebGPU; use the same small WebLLM models. Recommend Google AI Edge Gallery (Gemma 3n/4 E2B on 6 GB+ phones, E4B on 8 GB+), PocketPal or MLC Chat. Chrome's Gemini Nano Prompt API is not available on Android Chrome for web pages.
   - Rule: native GGUF model file ≤ ~50% of phone RAM.
2. Low-end laptop (≤8 GB RAM, integrated GPU, or Chromebook)
   - In the browser: WebLLM ≤3B q4 (Qwen3-1.7B, Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-3.5-mini-1k), or wllama/transformers.js WASM for ≤1B models, which will be slow.
   - Chrome's Gemini Nano needs more than 4 GB VRAM, or 16 GB RAM plus 4 cores, plus 22 GB free disk. Most low-end laptops fail this check, so say so explicitly.
   - Native: LM Studio needs AVX2 and recommends 16 GB. Ollama or Jan with 3-4B Q4 models (Qwen3-4B, Gemma-3-4B, Phi-4-mini, Llama-3.2-3B) is the realistic ceiling. 7-8B Q4 will be slow on 8 GB. whisper.cpp base/small models work fine.
3. Mac
   - Apple silicon: Chrome/Edge/Safari 26 WebGPU with f16 handles WebLLM up to about 60% of unified RAM (16 GB Mac: 8-9B q4f16 such as Qwen3.5-9B at 6.4 GB is WELL). Chrome Gemini Nano is available on macOS 13+ if the other requirements are met. Apple Foundation Models are built in on macOS 26+ with Apple Intelligence on.
   - Native install hints: 'brew install ollama', or LM Studio (macOS 14+, Apple silicon only), mlx-lm via 'pip install mlx-lm' for the fastest speed, Draw Things or ComfyUI Desktop for images, whisper.cpp with Core ML for speech.
   - RAM tiers: 8 GB means ≤4B; 16 GB means ≤14B Q4; 32 GB means ~30B / 30B-A3B MoE; 64-128 GB means 70B Q4, gpt-oss-120b and GLM/Qwen MoEs.
   - Intel Macs: CPU-only Ollama or llama.cpp. LM Studio is not supported. WebGPU exists but is weak.
4. Gaming PC (NVIDIA/AMD dGPU, 8-24 GB+ VRAM)
   - In the browser: Chrome/Edge WebGPU runs WebLLM up to VRAM × 0.7 (12 GB card: 8-9B models are WELL; the Llama-3.1-70B q3f16 at 31 GB is NOT AT ALL on anything under 32 GB+). Chrome Gemini Nano is available if VRAM is over 4 GB. Edge Phi-4-mini is only on Canary/Dev with 5.5 GB+ VRAM and a flag.
   - Native: Ollama or LM Studio (CUDA; AMD via ROCm v7 or Vulkan), with VRAM tiers of 8 GB for 7-8B Q4, 12-16 GB for 14B / 20B (gpt-oss-20b), and 24 GB for 27-32B Q4. With 64 GB+ system RAM, llama.cpp --cpu-moe lets 100B+ MoEs run SLOWLY.
   - ComfyUI for image and video: SDXL at 8 GB, Flux FP8 at 12-16 GB, Wan video at 12-24 GB.

Always show both 'run here in this browser now' (WebLLM, transformers.js, wllama, built-in LanguageModel) and 'install for better performance' (Ollama / LM Studio / mobile apps). Also link the ollama run commands.
